title: Model Catalog Demo - MountainCare
next_steps: Send model catalog PDF + compatibility matrix link
Share benchmark spreadsheet and raw latency/cost data
Provide SOC2 + network diagram to Dana
action_items: Priya Kapoor | Run quick latency baseline on their sample payloads and share results | Due: 2026-10-13
Jordan Lee | Send pricing tiers and dedicated capacity options | Due: 2026-10-08
Samir Patel | Provide sample prompt set and 1GB of anonymized logs for benchmarking | Due: 2026-10-12
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked MountainCare through the Model Catalog UI, selecting open models for conversational triage and summarization. Key discussion points: latency vs cost tradeoffs, hardware compatibility/quantization matrix, auto-batching behavior, prefix/KV cache implications, and enterprise security questions (SOC2, SSO, VPC). Agreement to run a 1-week POC to benchmark top model candidates with MountainCare prompts.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Header: 2026-10-06 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Kapoor (Redwood); Alex Morgan, Dana Price, Samir Patel (MountainCare)

00:00 Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 45 minutes, we'll do a quick intro and then jump into the model catalog demo.
00:08 Alex Morgan: yep sounds good, thanks jordan. we're mainly focused on using this for our patient triage chat and some summarization for clinical notes, so latency is pretty important.
00:16 Jordan Lee: got it, thanks. priya i'm gonna hand over to you to show the catalog and the perf profiles.
00:21 Priya Kapoor: cool thanks jordan, hi alex, dana, samir. i'm opening the model catalog now — you'll see filters on the left for task, latency tiers, and cost bands. we surface open models and our redwood-verified perf profile per model. quick note: some of the names in the catalog are community names, so sometimes they look diffr— uh different from the upstream project name.
00:40 Samir Patel: quick q — do you show quantized variants in the same card? or is that separate?
00:45 Priya Kapoor: we show variants inline; you'll see a dropdown on the model card for fp16, int8, and q4_0, q4_k which are our common quantization options. the perf profile shows real-world token/sec, median p95 lat, and recommended hardware mapping.
01:05 Dana Price: and the compatibility matrix you mentioned, where is that? like which GPUs and which runtime flags to use?
01:12 Priya Kapoor: good call, it's in the 'compatibility' tab per model. it lists supported GPUs (A100, H100, L40), recommended kernels, and notes on kv cache support and streaming. sometimes the transcriber/thing says K-V cash, haha, but it's KV cache.
01:30 Alex Morgan: laugh, yeah. ok can you show an example for a 13b model? that's our sweet spot for cost.
01:36 Priya Kapoor: sure — opening 'open-13b-chat-v2' card — here you can see baseline hosted latency on our smallest shared class, then a Dedicated profile with reserved throughput. note the quantized q4_0 variant drops p95 from ~420ms to ~300ms in our tests, and cost/unit decreases ~25%.
01:58 Samir Patel: those numbers — are they on A100 or on L40? i worry about mismatch.
02:03 Priya Kapoor: these are measured on A100 80GB; the compatibility matrix shows L40 tends to have slightly higher p95 for q4_0 due to kernel differences, but for long contexts L40 often wins on cost because of better memory packing.
02:22 Alex Morgan: how do you handle long prefix caching? our triage chat keeps context of prior messages — we need fast repeated replies for the same patient.
02:29 Priya Kapoor: we have prefix/KV caching — it's automatic for repeated prefixes and session affinity. for your use case we can cache the triage template and recent utterances which will drastically reduce token generation time. caveat: caching works best with associated sticky routing (session -> same instance) or with a shared KV layer we manage.
02:48 Dana Price: what's the privacy model for that cache? is it customer controlled?
02:52 Priya Kapoor: on Hosted the cache is in our managed infra but can be configured with TTLs and redaction. for Dedicated or Private you get customer-isolated caches and can run cache storage in your VPC. we can also integrate with your KMS for encryption at rest.
03:12 Samir Patel: about benchmarks — can we upload our prompt set and your team run benchmarks? or do we run them and share?
03:18 Jordan Lee: both options, we usually do a joint run for the POC; you'll send us sample prompts and we run them across 3-4 candidate models and return raw latency/cost spreadsheets.
03:28 Priya Kapoor: i'll annotate the compatibility matrix with recommended quantization for each model and which kernels to use. one note — sometimes the auto-quantized variants have small regressions on hallucination, so we recommend a quick quality check on your prompts.
03:45 Alex Morgan: good to know. what about multi-model fallback? if the primary model is down or too slow can we fall back to a cheaper smaller one?
03:52 Priya Kapoor: yes, routing policies support latency-based fallbacks and quality thresholds. in the console you can set a policy like: try open-13b-q4_0, if p95 > 800ms or error rate > 2% then route to open-7b-hf or a cached completion.
04:12 Dana Price: on security — we need SOC2 and network diagrams for our security review next week. can you send those?
04:18 Jordan Lee: absolutely, we'll share SOC2 report and a VPC/network diagram. priya, i'll need the consolidation of our private deployment notes.
04:25 Priya Kapoor: noted. we'll include KMS/HSM notes and SAML/SCIM SSO options. also RBAC for team-level token scoping.
04:35 Samir Patel: curious about cost — you mentioned cost bands; do you show per-token cost after batching effects?
04:41 Priya Kapoor: yes, the perf profile includes effective per-token cost estimates at different QPS and batching windows; note that batching improves cost but can worsen tail latency. we surface cost at small, medium, and high QPS scenarios.
04:58 Alex Morgan: could you run the numbers for our expected mix — 60% triage chat short prompts, 40% note summarization longer contexts?
05:05 Jordan Lee: we'll do that in the POC baseline — priya will run the workload simulation.
05:10 Priya Kapoor: on the console side i'll demo how we compare models — there's a 'compare' view where you pick up to 4 models and see p50/p95, token cost, and a compatibility heatmap.
05:22 Priya Kapoor: switching to the 'benchmarks' section — here we store our test harness results, raw latency histograms, and stress test runs. these are the same runs we use to generate the perf profile. note that community model names sometimes map to different forks, so we include git/commit-ish metadata when available.
05:41 Samir Patel: what about determinism and sampling — we need consistent top-k settings for reproducible triage answers. can you pin sampling parameters?
05:47 Priya Kapoor: yes, the API and console allow you to pin decoding params per route, including temperature, top_k, top_p, and seed for deterministic modes. also you can store route-specific prompt templates so inference is consistent.
06:05 Alex Morgan: any red flags for our infra — we're mostly on GCP with VPC peering, using KMS for keys.
06:12 Priya Kapoor: GCP peering is supported for Private deployments; Dedicated can be in partner cloud regions. for KMS we integrate via standard customer-managed keys, and audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
06:24 Dana Price: i want to see the compatibility matrix for H100 specifically — we have a couple of H100 reserved.
06:30 Priya Kapoor: yep i'll attach the H100 notes; quick point — some quantization kernels are still maturing on H100, you may see slightly different perf characteristics than A100 for q4_k kernels. we'll surface those per-model.
06:48 Samir Patel: about streaming — our UI needs streaming partial tokens for prompt-based triage to feel snappy. do you support streaming for quantized models?
06:55 Priya Kapoor: yes, streaming is supported across variants; quantized execution doesn't block streaming, but micro-batching may introduce small chunking behavior. we expose streaming granularities in the SDK.
07:10 Alex Morgan: any case studies for healthcare customers?
07:14 Jordan Lee: we have a few health systems using Redwood for summarization and patient message triage — we'll share anonymized references and a short deck.
07:22 Dana Price: ok great. let's talk about rollout — if we go Dedicated, what's the ramp timeline?
07:27 Jordan Lee: onboarding to Dedicated typically takes 4-6 weeks including infra provisioning and security reviews; Private/VPC deployments can be longer depending on approvals.
07:36 Priya Kapoor: and for the POC we usually do hosted first so we can iterate quickly, then move to Dedicated for scale.
07:44 Samir Patel: sounds sensible. any limitations on context length for the models you recommend?
07:49 Priya Kapoor: the catalog shows supported max context; open-13b-chat-v2 supports up to 16k in our tests for non-quantized, and about 8k comfortably for q4 variants depending on memory. again the compatibility matrix is the single place to check exact limits per quantization/hardware combo.
08:10 Alex Morgan: there's been mention of KV cache memory growth — how do you bound that?
08:15 Priya Kapoor: we enforce per-session TTL and size caps; for Dedicated we can expose metrics so you can set alerts if cache growth exceeds thresholds. also support truncation policies.
08:28 Dana Price: ok got it. one more on compliance — can you do HIPAA BAA?
08:33 Jordan Lee: we do BAA for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private deployments; we'll route this to legal but it's supported for qualifying customers.
08:40 Samir Patel: perfect.
08:42 Priya Kapoor: wrapping back to the demo — i'll show a quick export: pick two candidate models, compare quality on a sample prompt and then overlay perf.
08:50 Priya Kapoor: sample prompt: 'Patient describes chest pain, shortness of breath, list triage steps and flag red flags.' here's model A (open-13b-q4_0) output... [text snipped in transcript]
09:10 Samir Patel: output looks decent, how do you grade hallucination risk?
09:15 Priya Kapoor: we run automated checks comparing to a set of facts and also run human evals for the POC. our 'optimize' toolkit can run regression monitoring against your prompt set and send alerts on quality drift.
09:30 Alex Morgan: about that monitoring — can I get token-level cost mapping back to route and user id?
09:36 Priya Kapoor: yes, the console shows token-level breakdowns per-route and you can include metadata like user_id in the call so billing and traces map.
09:46 Dana Price: ok, that addresses our major items. next steps?
09:50 Jordan Lee: recap: we'll send model catalog export + compatibility matrix, share benchmarks, schedule POC kickoff with priya and samir, and provide SOC2 + network diagram.
09:59 Alex Morgan: will do on our side — samir will upload sample prompts.
10:05 Jordan Lee: great thanks all, we'll follow up over email with calendar invites.
10:10 Meeting end.
